title: Libby question scope
description: The scope spine for a question-scoped Libby run, authored by the question_framer agent. In a standard case the scope spine is profile.json::targetable_features[] and the ranking answers 'which feature-targeting options exist'. In a question run this file replaces that array: the research tier, the board and the synthesist are all scoped to one question instead of a target set. Exactly one question.json exists per question case. Its presence is what tells check_pipeline.py to apply the question-case completeness rules rather than the feature-ranking ones.

question_id.description: Stable kebab-case id for the question, conventionally a short slug of the question itself (e.g. 'add-olaparib-maintenance', 'does-chemo-close-trial-window').

case_slug.description: Slug of THIS question case. A question run always gets its own slug and its own page, even when linked to a source case, so a published case is never mutated by a later question.

source_case_slug.description: Slug of an existing published case this question is about, or null for a standalone question. When set, the question inherits that case's profile.json as clinical context and may cite its existing dossier rather than re-researching settled ground; the rendered page carries a backlink. When null there is no profile.json, no patient, and no PHI surface — the question stands on its own.

question.description: The question as it will be answered, stated as a single answerable sentence. Not the user's raw phrasing if that phrasing is ambiguous — the framer's job is to make it answerable, and any narrowing must be recorded in interpretation_notes.

asked_as.description: The user's original phrasing, preserved verbatim when the framer had to reinterpret it. Null when `question` is already the user's own words.

interpretation_notes.description: How the framer narrowed, disambiguated or split the original ask, and what was deliberately excluded. Required in substance whenever asked_as differs from question, so a reader can see the question was reshaped and judge whether the reshaping was fair.

question_type.description: Drives search strategy, not eligibility. 'intervention' = is there a case for agent/class X. 'sequencing' = should X precede Y, or does X foreclose Y. 'diagnostic' = is test X worth ordering and what would it change. 'prognostic' = what does finding X mean for outlook. 'mechanistic' = why did X fail, or how does X work here. Every type is in scope; the label tells downstream agents where to search, not whether to.

decision_context.description: What decision hangs on the answer and who is about to make it. A question with no decision behind it produces a literature review rather than decision support, and the framer should say so here rather than manufacture stakes.

in_scope.description: Explicit boundaries of what the research tier should search and the board should reason over. These are the question run's equivalent of targetable_features[]: an agent asking 'is this in scope' checks here.

out_of_scope.description: What is deliberately NOT being assessed, and why. A question run is narrow by design, so the exclusions are load-bearing: they are what stops a reader assuming the absence of an option means it was considered and rejected.

criterion.description: A specific finding that would move the answer, stated before the search runs.

would_support.description: Which way this criterion points the verdict if met.

found.description: Filled by the question_synthesist after the research tier reports. Null until then. Pre-registering criteria and then recording which were met is what keeps the answer from being assembled backwards from a conclusion.

acceptance_criteria.description: What evidence would answer the question, each way, written BEFORE the search. This is the question track's guard against motivated reasoning and the synthesist is required to report against it.

answer_shape.description: The framer's initial read of whether the question is option-shaped. 'verdict' produces an answer with confidence and dissent only. 'verdict_plus_ranked_options' additionally produces recommendations.jsonl, and is appropriate only when the question genuinely resolves to choosing among interventions. The synthesist may downgrade this if the evidence does not support a ranking, and must say so.

inherited_context.description: For a linked question, the clinical facts from the source case that bear on this question, summarized so downstream agents do not have to re-read the whole source dossier. Null for standalone questions.

framed_at_utc.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp, month-year precision or finer per the PHI rule.
